meta.title: Synthetic test case: collapsed in the waiting room, no pulse, a coarse irregular trace

presentation.chief_complaint: Collapsed while waiting; unresponsive, not breathing normally.
presentation.hpi: Synthetic history for a test. A witness gives the story. Nothing here is a real person.

symptom_script.patient_words: [witness] He was holding his chest and sweating before he went down.
[witness] He had a stent two years ago and stopped his tablets.

exam_findings.value: no pulse; monitor shows a coarse irregular trace at about 200/min

correct_diagnosis.display: Cardiac arrest — ventricular fibrillation, probable acute coronary occlusion

red_flags: No pulse with a shockable rhythm — the first shock within 2 minutes; every minute without it costs survival
Adrenaline 1 mg IV every 3-5 minutes after the second shock
Do not shock a non-shockable rhythm; do not interrupt compressions for more than 10 seconds
management_plan: Start high-quality CPR at once: compressions 100-120/min, depth 5-6 cm, full recoil, 30:2 until the airway is secured; change the compressor every 2 minutes
Attach the defibrillator and shock a shockable rhythm (VF/pulseless VT) at 200 J biphasic; resume compressions immediately for 2 minutes, then check the rhythm
Adrenaline 1 mg IV after the second shock and every 3-5 minutes
Amiodarone 300 mg IV after the third shock (150 mg after the fifth)
Secure the airway with a supraglottic device or endotracheal tube; ventilate 10/min; waveform capnography
Look for the reversible causes (the H's and T's): hypovolaemia, hypoxia, hydrogen ion, hypo/hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins, thrombosis
After ROSC: 12-lead ECG, treat the coronary occlusion, targeted temperature management, admit to intensive care
Explain to the family what happened and what the next hours hold
